title: €9 Plan Gone. Revenue +42%.
caption:
Two brothers took their €9 plan off the pricing page and revenue jumped 42% in a month.

The ladder was €9 / €49 / €99 on a B2B virus-scanning API. Sign-ups looked fine. What actually grew was support tickets and churn — €9 was buying developers on side projects. In the same move, they added €249 and €499 tiers.

I have a €9 tier. I added it because I was scared nobody would pay more, and I've been reading its sign-ups as traction ever since.

What's your cheapest plan?

slides.headline:
€9 Plan Gone.
Revenue +42%.
slides.sub: Two brothers pulled the €9 tier of their virus-scan API off the pricing page at the end of July. September revenue grew 42% over August. Churn is down to 4.9% and still falling.

slides.title: €9 Bought Side Projects
items: The ladder was Small €9, Medium €49, Large €99 — 10k, 50k and 100k requests a month.
Sign-ups looked healthy. Revenue rose slowly.
Support enquiries and churn were the only things growing.
€9 was selling to developers on side projects, not to businesses.

slides.headline:
Then They Added
€499
slides.sub: XL at €249 and XXL at €499 went up in the same move, topping out at 500,000 requests a month. Removing the floor was half of it.
